title: Fix sudo 'unable to resolve host' by adding the computer name to /etc/hosts
summary: sudo prints 'unable to resolve host' and may run slowly when the computer's name is missing from /etc/hosts. Adding one line with the name fixes it; sudo itself keeps working either way.

aliases.text: sudo warning unable to resolve host name
sudo hangs hostname not in hosts file
sudo name or service not known
sudo unable to resolve host ошибка
sudo долго работает имя компьютера не найдено

prerequisites: Know the name of your computer (step 1 shows it)

steps.explain: Show the name of your computer. sudo looks this name up in /etc/hosts; you need it for the next steps.
steps.expect: One word with no spaces, for example: laptop-ann. Write it down.

steps.explain: Look up the name in /etc/hosts. An empty output means the name is missing, which causes the warning. If a line with the name is printed, this card does not apply to your system: stop here.

placeholders.name: HOSTNAME
placeholders.description: The computer name printed by the hostname command

steps.expect: Empty output = name missing: go on. A line like '127.0.1.1 laptop-ann' = name found: this card does not apply.

steps.explain: Add a line that maps the name to the local address 127.0.1.1 at the end of /etc/hosts. tee -a appends the line, and it also prints the line back to you.

placeholders.name: HOSTNAME
placeholders.description: The computer name printed by the hostname command

steps.expect: The line 127.0.1.1 <name> is printed back. Your password is asked; typing stays hidden.

alternatives.explain: Edit the file by hand in the nano text editor: add the line 127.0.1.1 <HOSTNAME> at the end, press Ctrl+O and Enter to save, then Ctrl+X to exit.

placeholders.name: HOSTNAME
placeholders.description: The computer name printed by the hostname command

alternatives.expect: The nano editor opens /etc/hosts. After saving, the new line is in the file.

verify.expect: A line with 127.0.1.1 and your computer name, for example: 127.0.1.1 laptop-ann
Nothing printed: no 'unable to resolve host' warning. The password may be asked once.

rollback.explain: Remove the line you added in step 3 (it starts with 127.0.1.1). Open the file, delete that line, press Ctrl+O and Enter to save, then Ctrl+X to exit.

warnings: /etc/hosts is a system file. A wrong edit can break name lookups for other programs, so add only the one line and keep the spaces exact.
If you rename the computer later, the old name stays in /etc/hosts. Run this card again with the new name.
Some systems rewrite /etc/hosts at boot (for example cloud images), which removes the line and brings the warning back.
In our Fedora test the name resolved without this line and sudo printed no warning, so step 2 may already show the name on your system. Then nothing needs fixing.

source.title: sudo manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
